arxiv-2105-01253.title: The true mechanism of spontaneous order from turbulence in two-dimensional superfluid manifolds
arxiv-2105-01253.creator: Toshiaki Kanai, Wei Guo
arxiv-2105-01253.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Toshiaki Kanai, Wei Guo. In a two-dimensional (2D) turbulent fluid containing point-like vortices, Lars Onsager predicted that adding energy to the fluid can lead to the formation of persistent clusters of like-signed vortices, i.e., Onsager vortex (OV) clusters. In the evolution of 2D superfluid turbulence in a uniform disk-shaped Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), it was discovered that a pair of OV clusters with opposite signs can form without any energy input.

arxiv-2112-13243.title: Evolutionary Generation of Visual Motion Illusions
arxiv-2112-13243.creator: Lana Sinapayen 1† and Eiji Watanabe 2
arxiv-2112-13243.description: Abstract Why do we sometimes perceive static images as if they were moving? Visual motion illusions enjoy a sustained popularity, yet there is no definitive answer to the question of why they work. We present a generative model, the Evolutionary Illusion GENerator (EIGen), that creates new visual motion illusions.

arxiv-2205-07010.title: Inverse of α \alpha -Hermitian Adjacency Matrix of a Unicyclic Bipartite Graph
arxiv-2205-07010.creator: Mohammad Abudayah , Omar Alomari , Omar AbuGhneim
arxiv-2205-07010.description: Abstract Let X X be bipartite mixed graph and for a unit complex number α \alpha , H α H_{\alpha} be its α \alpha -hermitian adjacency matrix. If X X has a unique perfect matching, then H α H_{\alpha} has a hermitian inverse H α − 1 H_{\alpha}^{-1} .

arxiv-2206-00113.title: BRExIt: On Opponent Modelling in Expert Iteration
arxiv-2206-00113.creator: Daniel Hernandez, Hendrik Baier, Michael Kaisers
arxiv-2206-00113.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Daniel Hernandez, Hendrik Baier, Michael Kaisers. Finding a best response policy is a central objective in game theory and multi-agent learning, with modern population-based training approaches employing reinforcement learning algorithms as best-response oracles to improve play against candidate opponents (typically previously learnt policies). We propose Best Response Expert Iteration (BRExIt), which accelerates learning in games by incorporating opponent models into the state-of-the-art learning algorithm Expert Iteration (ExIt).

arxiv-2309-06531.title: ASPED: An Audio Dataset for Detecting Pedestrians
arxiv-2309-06531.creator: Pavan Seshadri, Chaeyeon Han, Bon-Woo Koo, Noah Posner, Subhrajit Guhathakurta, Alexander Lerch
arxiv-2309-06531.description: Abstract We introduce the new audio analysis task of pedestrian detection and present a new large-scale dataset for this task. While the preliminary results prove the viability of using audio approaches for pedestrian detection, they also show that this challenging task cannot be easily solved with standard approaches.

arxiv-2309-14312.title: Chow rings of matroids as permutation representations
arxiv-2309-14312.creator: Robert Angarone, Anastasia Nathanson, Victor Reiner
arxiv-2309-14312.description: Abstract . Given a matroid with a symmetry group, we study the induced group action on the Chow ring of the matroid with respect to symmetric building sets. This turns out to always be a permutation action. Work of Adiprasito, Huh and Katz showed that the Chow ring satisfies Poincaré duality and the Hard Lefschetz theorem.

arxiv-2408-09781.title: Neural Horizon Model Predictive Control - Increasing Computational Efficiency with Neural Networks
arxiv-2408-09781.creator: H. Alsmeier, A. Savchenko, R. Findeisen
arxiv-2408-09781.description: Abstract The expansion in automation of increasingly fast applications and low-power edge devices poses a particular challenge for optimization based control algorithms, like model predictive control. Our proposed machine-learning supported approach addresses this by utilizing a feed-forward neural network to reduce the computation load of the online-optimization.

arxiv-2502-05470.title: Kernel Smoothing for Bounded Copula Densities
arxiv-2502-05470.creator: Mathias Muia, Olivia Atutey, Mahmud Hasan
arxiv-2502-05470.description: Abstract Nonparametric estimation of copula density functions using kernel estimators presents significant challenges. One issue is the potential unboundedness of certain copula density functions at the corners of the unit square. Another is the boundary bias inherent in kernel density estimation. This paper presents a kernel-based method for estimating bounded copula density functions, addressing boundary bias through the mirror-reflection technique.

arxiv-2502-19189.creator: Jun-Rong Liu 1,2, Jian-Min Wang 1,2,3†, and S. Abdollahi 4, M. Ajello 5, R. Alves Batista 6, L. Baldini 7, C. Bartolini 8,9, D. Bastieri 10,11,12, J. Becerra Gonzalez 13, R. arxiv-2502-19189.description: Abstract Relativistic jets around supermassive black holes (SMBHs) are well-known powerful γ \gamma -ray emitters. In absence of the jets in radio-quiet active galactic nuclei (AGNs), how the SMBHs work in γ \gamma -ray bands is still unknown despite of great observational efforts made in the last 3 decades.

arxiv-2601-09702.title: Diagonalization Without Relativization A Closer Look at the Baker-Gill-Solovay Theorem
arxiv-2601-09702.creator: Baruch Garcia
arxiv-2601-09702.description: Abstract We already know that several problems like the inequivalence of P and EXP as well as the undecidability of the acceptance problem and halting problem relativize. However, relativization is a limited tool which cannot separate other complexity classes. What has not been proven explicitly is whether the Turing-recognizability of the acceptance problem relativizes.

Introduction Over half of eukaryotic proteins need to be translocated across at least one intracellular membrane to reach the final place of their function.

pmc-10573659.title: The Impact of Hydroxytyrosol on the Metallomic-Profile in an Animal Model of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-10573659.creator: Miguel Tabanez, Ilma R Santos, Juliane M Ikebara, Mariana L M Camargo, Bianca A Dos Santos, Bruna M Freire, Bruno L Batista, Silvia H Takada, Rosanna Squitti, Alexandre H Kihara, Giselle Cerchiaro, José Marco-Contelles
pmc-10573659.description: It is undeniable that as people get older, they become progressively more susceptible to neurodegenerative illnesses such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Memory loss is a prominent symptom of this condition and can be exacerbated by uneven levels of certain metals.

pmc-10642449.title: Proteomic analysis of peripheral nerve myelin during murine aging
pmc-10642449.creator: Dario Lucas Helbing, Joanna M. Kirkpatrick, Michael Reuter, Julia Bischoff, Amy Stockdale, Annemarie Carlstedt, Emilio Cirri, Reinhard Bauer, Helen Morrison
pmc-10642449.description: Aging of the peripheral nervous system (PNS) is associated with structural and functional changes that lead to a reduction in regenerative capacity and the development of age-related peripheral neuropathy. Myelin is central to maintaining physiological peripheral nerve function and differences in myelin maintenance, degradation, formation and clearance have been suggested to contribute to age-related PNS changes.

pmc-11318130.title: Outcomes of sutured scleral-fixated intraocular lens implantation combined with penetrating keratoplasty
pmc-11318130.creator: Abdulmohsen Almulhim, Waleed K Alsarhani, Bader Alanazi, Abdulrahman Alfaleh, Mohanna Aljindan, Rahaf M Al Malawi, Abdulaziz Al-Somali
pmc-11318130.description: BackgroundThe purpose of the study was to assess visual outcomes, complications, intraocular lens (IOL) stability, and corneal status after sutured scleral-fixated intraocular lens implantation combined with penetrating keratoplasty (PKP).MethodsThis retrospective single-arm cohort study included patients who underwent PKP and sutured scleral-fixated intraocular lens implantation between 2013 and 2018 at the Dhahran Eye Specialty Hospital.

pmc-11319146.title: A scientometrics analysis and visualization of refractory gastroesophageal reflux disease
pmc-11319146.creator: Nan Zhang, Ming Han, Qin-Wei Zheng, Meng-Yuan Zhang, Wen-Lan Zhi, Jing-Jing Li, Lin-Xuan Cui, Jin-Li Tian, Yi Wang, Sheng-Quan Fang
pmc-11319146.description: BackgroundRefractory gastroesophageal reflux disease (refractory GERD) is a heterogeneous disease characterized by unresponsiveness or poor efficacy to proton-pump inhibitors (PPIs). This chronic disorder substantially weakens patients’ mental wellbeing and quality of life, increasing the financial burden on society. Multiple articles have been reported in this area. However, literature involving scientometric analysis of refractory GERD is absent.

pmc-11321123.title: Clinical application research of intelligent monitoring system for knee rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11321123.creator: Wenqing Xie, Miao He, Shengyuan Zheng, Hengzhen Li, Hongfu Jin, Bingzhou Ji, Guang Yang, Yusheng Li
pmc-11321123.description: BackgroundThis study investigates the effectiveness of a self-developed intelligent monitoring system for home-based knee rehabilitation following total knee arthroplasty (TKA).MethodsIn this randomized controlled trial, 120 patients undergoing TKA were divided using random digit allocation. Preoperative and one-month postoperative assessments of knee function, quality of life, and isometric knee extension strength were conducted with the Intelligent Monitoring System.

pmc-11434458.title: Influence of Copper on Oleidesulfovibrio alaskensis G20 Biofilm Formation
pmc-11434458.creator: Payal Thakur, Vinoj Gopalakrishnan, Priya Saxena, Mahadevan Subramaniam, Kian Mau Goh, Brent Peyton, Matthew Fields, Rajesh Kumar Sani, Ute Römling
pmc-11434458.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Copper is known to have toxic effects on bacterial growth. This study aimed to determine the influence of copper ions on Oleidesulfovibrio alaskensis G20 biofilm formation in a lactate-C medium supplemented with variable copper ion concentrations. OA G20, when grown in media supplemented with high copper ion concentrations of 5, 15, and 30 µM, exhibited inhibited growth in its planktonic state. Conversely, under similar copper concentrations, OA G20 demonstrated enhanced biofilm formation on glass coupons.

pmc-11462660.title: Linking the reversal of gestational insulin resistance to postpartum depression
pmc-11462660.creator: Minoli Vinoda Abeysekera, Duan Ni, Leah Gilbert, Emily Hibbert, Ralph Nanan
pmc-11462660.description: BackgroundPostpartum depression (PPD) constitutes a significant mental health disorder affecting almost one fifth of pregnancies globally. Despite extensive research, the precise etiological mechanisms underlying PPD remain elusive. However, several risk factors like genetic predisposition, hormonal fluctuations, and stress-related environmental and psychosocial triggers have been found to be implicated in its development.

pmc-11523040.title: Considerations on Multimorbidity and Frailty in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
pmc-11523040.creator: Isabel Carbery, Christian P Selinger, Oliver Todd, Shaji Sebastian
pmc-11523040.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). There are growing numbers of older people with inflammatory bowel diseases [IBD]. These older patients are more likely to have other comorbidities and polypharmacy, which can make recognizing and treating IBD complex. Frailty is a newer concept in the IBD field, and we are beginning to recognize the importance of this as a marker of biological age and its association with risk of adverse IBD-related outcomes.

pmc-11580726.title: Role of mechanosensitive channel Piezo1 protein in intestinal inflammation regulation: A potential target
pmc-11580726.creator: Qinlei Jiang, Zhenyu Li, Dan Dang, Jiaqi Wei, Hui Wu
pmc-11580726.description: The intestine is a hollow tract that primarily transports and digests food. It often encounters mechanical forces and exotic threats, resulting in increased intestinal inflammation attributed to the consistent threat of foreign pathogens. Piezo1, a mechanosensitive ion channel, is distributed broadly and abundantly in the intestinal tissue.

pmc-11648077.title: Energetic Characteristics of Hydrophobic Porous Materials as Candidates for Manufacturing of Nanorockets
pmc-11648077.creator: Alexander
pmc-11648077.description: A new propulsion mechanism for nano- and microrocket engines is hypothesized. It is based on the instantaneous expulsion from hydrophobic nanopores triggered by irradiation from electromagnetic microwaves, ultrasound, or sudden pressure release. A large energy output is needed for the propulsion of a nanoparticle, and the value can be determined experimentally and by means of atomistic simulations.

pmc-11742124.title: Assessment of the financial gaps in cardiothoracic surgery in Africa
pmc-11742124.creator: Cynthia Nwalibe, Victory Bassey Effiom, Achanga Bill-Smith Anyinkeng, Michael Anayo James, Eben-Ezer Genda, Wambui Irungu, Frank-Awat Abaiweh, Kelechi E Okonta
pmc-11742124.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). OBJECTIVESThis study identified the challenges to financing cardiothoracic surgical care in Africa, highlighting the present state of funding and proffering probable solutions to adequate and effective funding in the region.METHODSIn a literature review, the authors elaborated key points, such as areas of financial funding in cardiothoracic surgery; barriers to appropriate allocation of financial resources for cardiothoracic surgery in Africa; and the needs and available resources for cardiothoracic surgery in Africa.

pmc-12403947.title: Comments on “heavy metals and their relationships with lung function and airway inflammation: insights from a population-based study”
pmc-12403947.creator: Tao Luo, Tao Chen
pmc-12403947.description: way inflammatory biomarkers for the first time. Using advanced statistical modeling, the authors assessed the independent and combined effects of various heavy metals while conducting detailed subgroup analyses across demographic populations. These findings contribute important epidemiological evidence linking heavy metal pollution to respiratory health risks, with implications for developing respiratory disease prevention strategies.

pmc-12534564.title: Nanostructured compact bulk MgB2 cryo-magnets with record-high critical currents and trapped magnetic fields
pmc-12534564.creator: Muralidhar Miryala, Tomoyuki Naito, Milos Jirsa, Jacques Noudem
pmc-12534564.description: We report a significant breakthrough in enhancing the performance of MgB₂ superconductors by engineering novel nanoscale defects using spark plasma sintering (SPS). By incorporating nanoscale MgB2O particles via silver addition, carbon doping, and magnesium excess, we introduce a transformative approach to defect design. This innovation yields exceptional material performance, characterized by a self-field critical current density (Jc) of 1.

pmc-12631720.title: Impact of Premature Birth and Delayed Cuddling on Maternal Support Needs and Satisfaction With Postnatal Care and Changes in Support Over Time
pmc-12631720.creator: Achim Fieß, Alica Hartmann, Alexander K Schuster, Stephanie D Grabitz, Dirk Wackernagel, Michael S Urschitz, Jonas Tesarz, Manfred E Beutel, Mareike Ernst, Eva Mildenberger, Sandra Gißler
pmc-12631720.description: BackgroundPreterm birth and early bonding disruptions such as delayed first cuddling may increase parental vulnerability and support needs in the postnatal period. However, little is known about how these factors interact to shape paternal perceptions of care and unmet support needs across different domains.

pmc-12693885.title: Reducing Risks in Petrochemical Plants Through the Integration of Existing and Emerging Gas Leak Detection Technologies
pmc-12693885.creator: Joon Hyuk Lee, Sung Yoon Lim, Jae Joon Lee, Hongjin Shin, Youngsik Kim, Inkwon Kim
pmc-12693885.description: Leakage of flammable gases and the resulting explosions in petrochemical plants remain latent risks, capable of occurring at any moment. Therefore, to address these worst-case scenarios within a virtual reality framework, we conducted simulations aimed at predicting and effectively responding to potential damages due to gas leakage.

pmc-13160564.creator: Emily T. Sturm, Anastasia G. Sares, Raana M. Manavi, Maiele E. Minzie, Jazmin M. Diaz, Andrea Mendez-Colmenares, John R. Duffy, Jason R. Tregellas, Don C. Rojas, Jared W. Young, Michael L. Thomas

pmc-13237235.title: Implications of Pr3+ ions on structural, opto-thermal features of alkali zinc boro-tellurite glass systems for optical and laser technology applications
pmc-13237235.creator: B. N. Shiva Kumar, C. Devaraja, G. V. Ashok Reddy, R. S. Gedam
pmc-13237235.description: A novel multicomponent series of Pr3+ -ions doped borotellurite glasses with composition (45-y)B2O3+20TeO2+20ZnO+5Pb3O4+10Na2O+yPr6O11, where y = 0.0, 0.3, 0.6, 1.0, 1.5, and 2 mol%, were prepared. ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy confirmed the presence of functional units, including BO4, BO3, TeO4, TeO3, and Pb–O and Zn–O links.

pmc-13297541.creator: Annalisa Magnani, Luca Bassi, Antonia Pierobon, Daniela Mancini, Valeria Torlaschi, Roberto Maestri, Pierluigi Chimento, Cira Fundarò, Marina Maffoni
pmc-13297541.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Standardized neuropsychological and psychological outcomes remained overall stable over time, with no significant differences between the intervention and control groups.Training-derived performance metrics showed variable, participant-specific patterns, with improvements in task speed observed in some cases. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13366906.title: Mental well-being, occupational stress, and caring behaviours among paediatric and psychiatric nurses in Slovenia
pmc-13366906.creator: Leona Cilar Budler, Tamara Trajbarič, Klavdija Čuček Trifkovič
pmc-13366906.description: BackgroundNursing is a demanding profession associated with elevated levels of occupational stress, which can negatively affect nurses’ mental well-being, job satisfaction, and capacity for caring behaviour. Paediatric and psychiatric nurses face distinct stressors related to their work environments and patient populations.

pmc-13403432.title: Speech Depression Screening via Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement and Emotion-Aware Contrastive Learning
pmc-13403432.creator: Zhengyuan Chen, Meihong Wu
pmc-13403432.description: Speech-based depression screening is a promising non-invasive approach, but short spontaneous-speech segments often contain weak acoustic cues, fragmented semantic context, and overlapping representations between depressed and non-depressed participants. This study addresses this problem by proposing a preliminary short-segment acoustic screening framework that integrates multi-scale feature enhancement and reference-enhanced contrastive calibration. Based on the self-supervised pretrained Wav2Vec 2.
